title.en: UV atlas and source-to-target bake correspondence

summary: Make seams, UV-set roles, island scale, projection cage and padding explicit so a high-detail source bakes repeatably onto the exact low-detail mesh exported to glTF.
objective: The imported low mesh samples the intended atlas without overlaps, projection leaks, visible mip seams, or a bake that no longer corresponds to delivered topology.
applies_when: A low-detail glTF mesh receives baked texture data from a separate high-detail source or uses multiple UV sets with distinct roles.
intent_signals: high poly details project onto wrong part
example_prompts: Prepare a low-poly vehicle atlas from a high-poly source with stable padding and a documented second UV set.
Fix seams that appear only when a baked prop recedes in the Three.js camera.
negative_signals: Mirror tangent normal maps without the rendering contract
Pack islands before freezing delivery topology
not_for: Runtime tangent-space normal-map handedness or UV-mirror interpretation; those belong to the rendering handoff.
Procedural triplanar materials that deliberately use no UV atlas.

principles: A bake is a correspondence from source surface samples to target UV texels. The target mesh, UV map, cage and source selection together define that correspondence.
Texel density and padding solve different problems: island scale allocates resolution, while gutter pixels protect filtering and mip levels at island boundaries.
UV-set roles must cross the boundary by index. Name maps for humans, but inspect which TEXCOORD_n each glTF texture actually references.
implementation: Freeze the target object's evaluated topology before final unwrap and bake. Mark seams at hidden or natural boundaries, minimize stretch, then use Average Island Scale as a starting point and override only for explicitly prioritized surfaces.

Pack the delivery UV set into the intended tile with a margin derived from the lowest expected mip, atlas resolution and filtering. Keep intentional overlaps in a separately documented set or isolate them before baking unique detail.

Use Selected to Active with the low target active and only the approved high source selected. Choose extrusion/max ray distance or an explicit cage; if using a cage copy, preserve the target face count and face order.

Bake an identification pass before expensive maps: assign distinct source-region colors and verify that every low-mesh island receives the expected source. Then bake production data without changing target topology, UVs or cage.

Export all required UV maps and inspect the GLB's TEXCOORD indices and material texCoord references. Three.js owns texture assignment and sampling; the asset owns vertex UV coordinates and texture-to-set selection.
Test the imported atlas close up and at receding distances against a high-contrast seam chart; log any intentional density exception.
observable_checks: A checker has comparable scale on equal-priority surfaces and reveals no unintended overlap or severe stretch.
The source-region identification bake lands on the correct target parts without projection from the opposite side or neighbouring component.
At distant mip levels, island boundaries remain free of unrelated color bleed; GLB inspection confirms the expected TEXCOORD_n per texture role.

creative_affordances: Allocate more texels to faces users inspect and fewer to hidden undersides when the exception is documented.
Use a second non-overlapping set for baked data while retaining a tiled set for repeated surface detail.
known_limits: Padding needs depend on resolution, filtering, compression and the minimum displayed mip.
This record deliberately does not govern normal-map tangent basis or mirrored-UV handedness.
Authored reusable guidance; no bake, export, import or runtime artifact was executed for this record.

claims.statement: Blender's UV tools can approximately equalize island scale and pack islands with a specified margin; Cycles Selected to Active projects from selected source objects to the active target using ray distance, extrusion or a cage, requires a cage copy to keep the same topology and face order, and generates margin around UV islands to reduce filtering and mipmap seam discontinuities.
claims.scope: Blender 4.5 UV and Cycles bake controls; required numerical margins and artistic seam placement remain authored decisions.

source_refs.locator: Average Island Scale; Pack Islands; Minimize Stretch

claims.statement: glTF texture information selects a texture-coordinate attribute by integer texCoord index, while Blender's exporter can include UV attributes and warns that discontinuous UVs can split exported vertices.
claims.scope: glTF 2.0 texture-coordinate selection plus Blender 4.5 exporter behavior; it does not define tangent-space interpretation.

source_refs.locator: Texture Info; Meshes > Mesh Primitives > TEXCOORD_n
